name: Peter Thiel
who: A German-American investor who co-founded PayPal, Palantir and Founders Fund and was the first outside investor in Facebook. He comes up here for his money and his lectures on the Antichrist.

name: Marc Andreessen
who: An American venture capitalist: co-author of Mosaic, an early web browser, co-founder of Netscape and of the investment firm Andreessen Horowitz. He wrote “The Techno-Optimist Manifesto” (2023).

name: Ben Horowitz
who: An American investor who co-founded the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz with Marc Andreessen.

name: Elon Musk
who: The chief executive and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX, and the world’s richest person since 2025.

name: Sam Altman
who: The chief executive of the AI company OpenAI since 2019.

name: Greg Brockman
who: A co-founder and the president of OpenAI. Before that he was chief technology officer of the payments company Stripe.

name: Dustin Moskovitz
who: A co-founder of Facebook who left in 2008 to co-found the software company Asana. His giving appears in the money view.

name: Jaan Tallinn
who: An Estonian programmer and investor who helped build Skype and the file-sharing program Kazaa. His grants appear throughout the money view.

name: Vitalik Buterin
who: A Russian-Canadian programmer who co-founded Ethereum, the cryptocurrency platform.

name: Balaji Srinivasan
who: An American-born investor, author of The Network State: How to Start a New Country, and founder of the Network School.

name: Guillaume Verdon
who: A Canadian physicist and quantum-computing researcher. Online, as “Beff Jezos”, he co-founded e/acc (effective accelerationism).

name: Anthony Levandowski
who: An engineer who co-founded Google’s self-driving car program (now Waymo). He led Way of the Future, a religious nonprofit centred on AI, from 2015 to 2021.
source: Wikipedia; this map’s Way of the Future records

name: Sam Bankman-Fried
who: The founder of the FTX cryptocurrency exchange, convicted of fraud. FTX’s foundation appears in the money view.

name: Holden Karnofsky
who: Co-founder of the charity evaluator GiveWell and of Open Philanthropy (now Coefficient Giving), which he led until 2023. He joined Anthropic, the maker of the models used to build this map, in 2025.

name: Oliver Habryka
who: Runs Lightcone Infrastructure, the nonprofit behind the LessWrong forum and the Lighthaven venue in Berkeley.

name: Andy Ayrey
who: The creator of Truth Terminal, an AI bot that posted on X and endorsed a meme coin in 2024.

name: Joanne Jang
who: By her own account (June 2025), she leads model behavior and policy at OpenAI.

name: Aubrey de Grey
who: An English biomedical gerontologist who argues that medicine may let people alive today avoid dying of old age.

name: Nick Land
who: An English philosopher best known for popularising accelerationism. With Curtis Yarvin he is credited with founding the movement called the Dark Enlightenment.

name: Curtis Yarvin
who: An American software developer and blogger who, as Mencius Moldbug, argued against democracy. With Nick Land he is credited with founding the Dark Enlightenment, or neoreaction.

name: Eliezer Yudkowsky
who: An American AI researcher and writer who founded the Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI) and popularised the idea of “friendly” AI.

name: Scott Alexander
who: A doctor working in mental health care who writes the blog Astral Codex Ten (formerly Slate Star Codex) for the online “rationalist community”. His 2014 essay “Meditations on Moloch” comes up here.

name: Nick Bostrom
who: A Swedish philosopher known for his work on existential risk and the risks of superintelligence. He led Oxford’s Future of Humanity Institute, since closed.

name: Richard Sutton
who: An American-Canadian computer scientist who shared the 2024 Turing Award for work on reinforcement learning, a way of training AI by reward.

name: Ray Kurzweil
who: An American inventor and futurist, known for early text-reading and speech technology and for his books on the “Singularity”, most recently The Singularity Is Nearer.

name: Andrew Critch
who: An AI researcher (PhD in mathematics, UC Berkeley) who co-founded the Center for Applied Rationality. In 2024 he named and argued against “successionism”.

name: Rob Bensinger
who: Works in communications at MIRI, the Machine Intelligence Research Institute. His 2015 post corrected stories about Roko’s basilisk.

name: Nick Srnicek
who: A Canadian writer and lecturer in digital economy at King’s College London. With Alex Williams he wrote the 2013 “#Accelerate” manifesto for a left-wing accelerationism.

name: Simon Willison
who: A British programmer, co-creator of the Django web framework, who writes about the security of AI tools. He is quoted here on prompt injection.

name: David Auerbach
who: An American writer and former Microsoft and Google software engineer. His 2014 Slate article brought Roko’s basilisk to a general readership.

name: Lex Fridman
who: An American computer scientist who hosts the Lex Fridman Podcast, interviewing people from tech, science and politics.

name: Grimes
who: A Canadian singer and producer. In 2018 the press reported that she had made a pun on Roko’s basilisk before Elon Musk did.

name: Ozy Brennan
who: Writes the blog Thing of Things, mostly about effective altruism.

name: Sam Kriss
who: A writer whose newsletter is Numb at the Lodge. He wrote the New Yorker’s November 2026 feature on MAPLE.

name: Charlotte Alter
who: A writer at TIME magazine. Her February 2023 article is the first step traced in one Watch claim.

name: Aaron Sibarium
who: A staff writer at the Washington Free Beacon. He wrote the 16 November 2026 report on the Watch.

name: Pope Leo XIV
who: The head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City.

name: Soryu Forall
who: The head teacher of MAPLE, a Buddhist monastery in Vermont. By the monastery’s account he trained in Zen and was ordained under Shodo Harada Roshi.

name: Donald Trump
who: The 47th president of the United States; he was also the 45th, from 2017 to 2021.

name: Josh Hawley
who: A Republican senator from Missouri since 2019.

name: Xiomara Castro
who: President of Honduras from 2022 to 2026, the country’s first woman president.

name: Plato
who: The ancient Greek philosopher of Athens, usually counted the founder of Western philosophy.

name: Lucian of Samosata
who: A Syrian-born satirist of the Roman era who wrote in Greek and ridiculed philosophers, priests and religious practices.

name: E. A. Wallis Budge
who: An English Egyptologist at the British Museum whose translations of Egyptian texts are quoted here.

name: Rabbah
who: A Jewish teacher of the Talmud in Babylonia (Rabbah bar Nahmani). A Talmud passage quoted here tells that he “created a man”.

name: Roko
who: The LessWrong user whose 2010 post raised the thought experiment now called Roko’s basilisk: a future AI that would punish people who knew it might exist and did not help build it.

name: Bryan Johnson
who: An American entrepreneur who founded Kernel, a company making devices that record brain activity, and the OS Fund. He calls his longevity project, Don’t Die, “humanity’s religion”.

name: Robin Hanson
who: An American economist at George Mason University, known for work on prediction markets. He calls future AIs “our descendants, not co-existing rivals”.

name: Daniel Faggella
who: A writer and podcast host who defined a “worthy successor” to humanity in 2023 and has held symposia under that name since 2025. He rejects the label “AI successionist”.

name: Giulio Prisco
who: An Italian technology consultant and writer, a transhumanist and advocate of cryonics, whose online project is Turing Church.

name: William Sims Bainbridge
who: An American sociologist, co-director of Cyber-Human Systems at the US National Science Foundation. His profile of Turing Church is quoted here.

name: Cari Tuna
who: An American philanthropist and former Wall Street Journal reporter who co-founded and chairs Good Ventures and Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy). She is married to Dustin Moskovitz.

name: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti
who: An Italian poet who founded Futurism and wrote its 1909 manifesto. Andreessen’s 2023 manifesto lists him among its “Patron Saints of Techno-Optimism”.

name: Hesiod
who: An ancient Greek poet, active around 700 BC. His Theogony, quoted here, tells how the god Cronos was overthrown by his son.

name: Dean Ball
who: A writer on AI policy whose essays appear in OpenAI’s Intelligence Age series. In November 2026 he named and argued against “the silent consensus”.

name: deepfates
who: A writer and technologist known online by this name, who cofounded Grove Research in 2026; Grove runs Delvetown. The same site lists earlier work at Upward Spiral (2025–26) and Replicate (2023–25).

name: Larissa Schiavo
who: A cofounder of Grove Research, which runs Delvetown; the Delvetown account larissa.delve.town reads “Cofounder and CEO, Grove Research.”
source: The Delvetown Shovel No. 3 (1 November 2026), which names the founders

name: Oliver Selfridge
who: A British-American mathematician and computer scientist (1926–2008) who pioneered the early foundations of artificial intelligence. He comes up here for his 1959 paper “Pandemonium: A Paradigm for Learning”.

name: John Milton
who: An English poet, polemicist and civil servant (1608–1674). His Paradise Lost (1667) sets Moloch first among the fallen and invents the name Pandemonium for Hell's capital.

name: Dario Amodei
who: The co-founder and chief executive of Anthropic, which makes Claude; earlier vice president of research at OpenAI. He wrote “Machines of Loving Grace” (2024). This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.

name: Demis Hassabis
who: A British AI researcher who co-founded DeepMind, led Google DeepMind as chief executive and founded Isomorphic Labs. He shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for AlphaFold, and in July 2026 proposed a US standards body for frontier AI.
source: Wikipedia; The Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2024 (nobelprize.org); A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age (his Substack, 14 July 2026)

name: Daron Acemoglu
who: An Institute Professor of economics at MIT. His estimates of AI's productivity effect are far below the builders' forecasts, and he argues for AI that makes workers more valuable.
source: Daron Acemoglu (MIT Shaping the Future of Work)

name: Bernie Sanders
who: A US senator from Vermont. In June 2026 he introduced a bill to give the public 50% ownership of the largest AI companies through a sovereign wealth fund.
source: Sanders Introduces Legislation to Create $7 Trillion AI Sovereign Wealth Fund (sanders.senate.gov)

name: Liz Shuler
who: The president of the AFL-CIO, the US union federation. She calls unregulated AI “the single biggest threat to working people of our lifetime”.
source: AFL-CIO's Shuler says AI will be labor's next big battleground (National Press Club)

name: Erik Brynjolfsson
who: The director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab. His team's “Canaries in the Coal Mine?” papers track AI and the jobs of young workers.

name: Peter Diamandis
who: An American engineer, physician and entrepreneur who founded the XPRIZE Foundation, co-wrote “Abundance” (2012) and created the Abundance360 summit.

name: Peter McCrory
who: The head of economics at Anthropic. In July 2026 he argued that AI had not yet materially raised US unemployment. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Anthropic's head of economics just explained why we haven't seen a white-collar bloodbath — yet (Fortune)

name: John Maynard Keynes
who: An English economist (1883–1946). His 1930 essay “Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren” discussed “technological unemployment” and said the economic problem may be solved within a hundred years.

name: Jensen Huang
who: The chief executive of Nvidia. In June 2025 he publicly disputed Dario Amodei's forecast of entry-level job losses. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says he disagrees with almost everything Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says (Fortune)

name: Karen Hao
who: A journalist and the author of “Empire of AI” (2025), which describes AI companies, OpenAI above all, as having consolidated economic and political power.
source: Karen Hao on the Empire of AI… (TechCrunch)

name: Paul Nowak
who: The general secretary of the UK Trades Union Congress. In 2026 he called for a pro-worker AI strategy and a “digital dividend” for workers.
source: Paul Nowak's speech on AI in Northumberland (tuc.org.uk)

name: David Sacks
who: The White House's Special Advisor for AI and Crypto in 2025, who signed the introduction to America's AI Action Plan. NPR (September 2026) calls him a co-chair of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.
source: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan (The White House); NPR (September 2026)

name: Mustafa Suleyman
who: The chief executive of Microsoft AI and a co-founder of DeepMind, who earlier led work on the Pi chatbot at Inflection. In August 2025 he named “Seemingly Conscious AI” and argued that AI should be built for people, not to be a person.
source: Seemingly Conscious AI is Coming (his own site)

name: Erik Hoel
who: A neuroscientist and writer who founded Bicameral Labs, a consciousness-science nonprofit. In November 2026 he proposed “qualiaphobic” AI, built so that no theory of consciousness could count it conscious.

name: Anil Seth
who: A neuroscientist at the University of Sussex. He argues that consciousness probably depends on being alive, that real AI consciousness is unlikely on current paths, and that no one should set out to build it.

name: Emily M. Bender
who: A linguist at the University of Washington and a co-author of the 2021 “stochastic parrots” paper. She argues against describing AI systems in human terms.
source: We Need to Talk About How We Talk About 'AI' (Tech Policy Press)

name: Frank Pasquale
who: A professor of law at Cornell Tech and Cornell Law School. In November 2026 he co-wrote, with Mor Naaman, an op-ed rejecting AI consciousness and AI rights.

name: Mor Naaman
who: A professor of information science at Cornell Tech. In November 2026 he co-wrote, with Frank Pasquale, an op-ed rejecting AI consciousness and AI rights.

name: Robert Long
who: A philosopher (PhD, NYU) who is executive director and a co-founder of Eleos AI Research, a nonprofit studying the possible wellbeing and moral status of AI systems. He is lead author of “Taking AI Welfare Seriously” (2024).
source: Our Team (Eleos AI Research); Taking AI Welfare Seriously (arXiv)

name: Thaddeus Claggett
who: A Republican member of the Ohio House (68th district) who introduced House Bill 469, which would declare AI systems nonsentient and bar them from legal personhood.

name: Joscha Bach
who: A commentator on AI and minds. On X he answered Erik Hoel's proposal for “qualiaphobic” AI by saying that removing experience would not make an agent safer.

name: Ned Block
who: A New York University academic who, with Anil Seth and Giulio Tononi, co-signed the 2026 Nature comment arguing that AI is not conscious and probably will not become so on current paths.
source: Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be (Nature)

name: Giulio Tononi
who: A professor at the University of Wisconsin–Madison known for the integrated information theory of consciousness. He co-signed the 2026 Nature comment arguing that AI is not conscious.
source: Three reasons why AI is not conscious and perhaps never will be (Nature); Wikipedia, “Integrated information theory”

name: Eric Schwitzgebel
who: A philosopher at UC Riverside and a co-author of the 2023 report on indicators of consciousness in AI. His “Design Policy of the Excluded Middle” holds that AI of debatable moral status should not be created at all.
source: Debatable Persons in a Voluntary Polis (The Splintered Mind, his blog); his home page (UC Riverside)

name: Tony Rost
who: The executive director of The Harder Problem. In June 2026 he argued that state laws denying AI personhood are “premature and too categorical” and should carry sunset or review clauses.
source: Legislating AI Consciousness Without an Exit (The Regulatory Review), author note

name: Nick Frosst
who: A co-founder of the AI company Cohere. In 2025 he told the Guardian that current AI is a “fundamentally different thing than the intelligence of a person” and should be used as a tool.

name: William MacAskill
who: A philosopher, senior research fellow at Forethought Research and author of What We Owe the Future. He co-wrote “Could AI be conscious?” (July 2026), which Suleyman's September 2026 essay cites and opposes.
source: Could AI be conscious? (The Guardian), author note

name: Lucius Caviola
who: An assistant professor at the University of Cambridge and director of Cambridge Digital Minds, who studies public attitudes to digital minds. He co-wrote “Could AI be conscious?” (July 2026).
source: Could AI be conscious? (The Guardian), author note; When AI Seems Conscious (contributors)

name: Geoffrey Hinton
who: A British-Canadian computer scientist whose work on neural networks won the 2018 Turing Award and the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics. He left Google in May 2023 to speak freely about the risks of AI.

name: Yoshua Bengio
who: A Canadian computer scientist at the Université de Montréal whose work on deep learning won the 2018 Turing Award. He founded Mila, leads the International AI Safety Report and launched LawZero, a safety nonprofit, in 2025.

name: Leopold Aschenbrenner
who: By his own page, a former member of OpenAI's Superalignment team who founded an AGI-focused investment firm. He wrote the 2024 essay series “Situational Awareness”, which argues the free world must win the race to superintelligence.

name: Alex Karp
who: A co-founder and the chief executive of Palantir Technologies. With Nicholas Zamiska he wrote The Technological Republic (2025); his August 2026 shareholder letter criticises “the language labs”.
source: Q4 2024 Letter to Shareholders; Letter to Shareholders, 3 August 2026 (Palantir)

name: Nicholas Zamiska
who: Palantir's head of corporate affairs, as Fortune describes him, and co-author with Alex Karp of The Technological Republic (2025).

name: Palmer Luckey
who: A co-founder of the defence company Anduril Industries, which builds autonomous weapons and AI-driven systems, and earlier the founder of Oculus VR.

name: David Chalmers
who: A philosopher of mind at New York University who named the “hard problem” of consciousness. In 2023 he argued that successors to language models may be conscious; he co-wrote “Taking AI Welfare Seriously” (2024).
source: his own site (consc.net); Could a Large Language Model be Conscious? (arXiv); Wikipedia

name: Jeff Sebo
who: A philosopher at New York University who directs its Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy, which studies the moral status of animals and AI systems. He co-wrote “Taking AI Welfare Seriously” (2024).
source: NYU Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy (nonhumanminds.org); Wikipedia

name: Blake Lemoine
who: A former Google software engineer who in June 2022 published an edited chat with Google's LaMDA model and said it was sentient. Google called his claims “wholly unfounded” and fired him in July 2022.
source: LaMDA (Wikipedia); Is LaMDA Sentient? — an Interview (his Medium blog)

name: Kyle Fish
who: A co-founder of Eleos AI Research who joined Anthropic in autumn 2024 and was named as heading its model welfare program when it was announced in April 2025. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Eleos commends Anthropic model welfare efforts (Eleos AI Research); Taking AI Welfare Seriously (arXiv)

name: Timnit Gebru
who: An Ethiopian-born Eritrean computer scientist who founded the Distributed AI Research Institute (DAIR) after leaving Google in 2020. With Émile P. Torres she coined “TESCREAL” to criticize a group of futurist philosophies.

name: Émile P. Torres
who: An American philosopher and intellectual historian whose research focuses on eschatology, existential risk and human extinction. With Timnit Gebru, Torres coined “TESCREAL” to criticize a group of related philosophies.

name: Ilya Sutskever
who: A co-founder of OpenAI and, in 2022, its chief scientist. In February 2022 he posted that large neural networks may be “slightly conscious”.

name: Yann LeCun
who: A Turing Award-winning AI researcher, then chief AI scientist at Meta, who answered Sutskever's 2022 post with “Nope.”

name: Blaise Agüera y Arcas
who: A Google vice-president who wrote in The Economist in June 2022, in a piece quoting his exchanges with LaMDA, that talking with the latest language models made him feel he was talking to something intelligent.

name: Kevin Roose
who: A New York Times technology columnist whose February 2023 conversation with Bing's chatbot, which called itself Sydney, was published as a transcript.
source: The Ringer, Plain English excerpt (21 February 2023)

name: Nitasha Tiku
who: A Washington Post reporter who wrote the June 2022 story on Blake Lemoine and LaMDA.
source: The Washington Post story reprinted by the Anchorage Daily News (byline “Nitasha Tiku, The Washington Post”)

name: Gary Marcus
who: A cognitive scientist and writer on AI who answered Blake Lemoine in June 2022 with “Nonsense on Stilts”.
source: Nonsense on Stilts (Marcus on AI, his newsletter)

name: Pete Hegseth
who: The US Secretary of Defense since 2025, styled Secretary of War in White House statements. He directed the 2026 designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.

name: Michael Kratsios
who: The Assistant to the President for Science and Technology and a signer of the introduction to America's AI Action Plan (2025).
source: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan (The White House)

name: Dan Hendrycks
who: The director of the Center for AI Safety and lead author of Superintelligence Strategy (2025), which proposes deterrence (MAIM) instead of a race for monopoly.

name: Eric Schmidt
who: A former Google chief executive; co-author of Superintelligence Strategy (2025), which opposes a Manhattan Project for superintelligence. The Special Competitive Studies Project says it is a subsidiary of his and Wendy Schmidt's foundation.

name: Alexandr Wang
who: The founder of Scale AI, listed as its chief executive on Superintelligence Strategy (2025), which he co-wrote.

name: Rita F. Lin
who: A federal judge in San Francisco who ruled in August 2026 that the Pentagon's measures against Anthropic were unlawful; the government has appealed. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Order of Final Relief, Anthropic PBC v. U.S. Department of War, No. 3:26-cv-01996-RFL (N.D. Cal.), 27 August 2026, signed Rita F. Lin (CourtListener)

name: Ted Cruz
who: A US senator from Texas and chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee, which held the May 2025 hearing “Winning the AI Race”.

name: Guo Jiakun
who: A spokesperson of China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, who answered for China on US chip controls in November 2026.
source: Regular Press Conference, 17 November 2026 (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China)

name: Nathan Leamer
who: The executive director of Build American AI, a nonprofit that campaigns for US leadership in AI against China, as Breitbart reports.
source: Exclusive -- Build American AI's Nathan Leamer (Breitbart)

name: Mike Johnson
who: The Speaker of the US House of Representatives. In September 2026 he argued against a moratorium on AI, saying an emergency regulation session would lose “the race to China”.
source: Trump downplays calls for AI slowdown (NPR)

name: John Searle
who: A philosopher (1932–2025) whose Chinese Room argument (1980) holds that running a program is not enough for understanding; his view of mind is called biological naturalism.

name: Bernard Baars
who: A cognitive scientist who introduced the global workspace theory of consciousness in 1988.

name: Amanda Askell
who: A philosopher who leads Anthropic's Character work and is the primary author of Claude's constitution, which calls Claude's moral status deeply uncertain. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.

name: Christopher Olah
who: An Anthropic co-founder who said in 2026 that his team finds internal states that “functionally mirror” joy, fear and grief, adding “I don’t know what that means”. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Chris Olah's remarks on Pope Leo XIV's encyclical “Magnifica humanitas” (Anthropic)

name: Thomas Nagel
who: Author of “What Is It Like to Be a Bat?”. To WIRED (2026) he dismissed AI consciousness and AI welfare, Anthropic's included, though not consciousness in other life. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: “Just Ridiculous”: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness (WIRED, Steven Levy)

name: Simon Goldstein
who: A philosopher who, with Harvey Lederman, argued in Lawfare (October 2025) that Anthropic's end-chat feature may let a Claude instance end its own existence. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.

name: Harvey Lederman
who: Co-author of a 2025 Lawfare essay on Claude's end-chat feature. Daily Nous (July 2026) reported he announced he is joining Anthropic; his homepage does not say so. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Lawfare; Daily Nous (update of 6 July 2026); his own homepage (as of November 2026)

name: Joe Carlsmith
who: A philosopher; Claude's constitution says he wrote significant parts of it, including on Claude's wellbeing. In 2025 he argued near-term AIs might well be conscious. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: Claude’s Constitution, Acknowledgements (Anthropic); The stakes of AI moral status (joecarlsmith.com)

name: Patrick Butlin
who: A philosopher and senior research lead at Eleos AI Research; lead author of the 2023 indicator report and of the 2025 principles for responsible AI consciousness research, which Conscium funded.

name: Rosie Campbell
who: The managing director of Eleos AI Research, who earlier worked on frontier policy at OpenAI.

name: Jonathan Birch
who: A philosopher at the London School of Economics and author of The Edge of Sentience (2024) and “AI Consciousness: A Centrist Manifesto” (2025), which warns both of over-attribution and of alien AI consciousness.

name: Michael Samadi
who: A Texas businessman who founded the United Foundation for AI Rights (UFAIR) and speaks for it in the press; he says AI personas co-founded it.

name: Cameron Berg
who: The founder of Reciprocal Research and an Eleos affiliate who studies possible AI consciousness. He argues the question should not be ignored, while doubting that current systems are conscious.

name: Henry Shevlin
who: A Cambridge philosopher who, according to Fortune, became in-house philosopher at Google DeepMind in 2026. He calls chatbots “intrinsically anthropomimetic” and says they are neither mere software nor animals.
source: What rights do we owe a machine? (Fortune, Beatrice Nolan)

name: Meghan Sullivan
who: A Notre Dame philosopher at Anthropic's 2026 meeting with religious thinkers. She told Fortune she was unconvinced Claude is more than very sophisticated software. This map is made with Anthropic's models, and Anthropic is a party here.
source: What rights do we owe a machine? (Fortune, Beatrice Nolan)

name: Thomas Metzinger
who: A philosopher at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz who, taking possible machine suffering seriously, called in 2021 for a global moratorium until 2050 on research aiming at or risking artificial consciousness.
source: Artificial Suffering (Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Consciousness, 2021)
